answer.rationale: Primary expires in 14 days with no auto-renew and the line is at 94% with no buffer, so the one decision must keep supply continuous while attacking TCO. Incumbent refusal was to reopen this cycle; c4 says the renewal event itself is when benchmarking moved price and terms, and c6 says a longer commitment unlocked volume pricing without shrinking scope. That path preserves the integration stability in c1. Switching on c2 could cut unit cost but onboarding a new primary into a no-buffer, 14-day window increases delivery risk and violates the objective. Second-source or defer leave the expiring primary unaddressed under a one-action constraint. Downstream disruption risk is flagged; it is uncertain whether an 18% move is achievable.
